s: How should EC2 instances in AWS synchronize their clocks with an on-premisesatomic clock NTP server, with the least administrative overhead?
o: Configure a DHCP options set with the on-prem NTP server.
Use a custom AMI with Amazon Time Sync.
Deploy a 3rd-party NTP server from Marketplace.
Create an IPsec VPN tunnel to sync over Direct Connect.
e: Option Ais the most lightweight and scalable approach. By updating the VPC'sDHCP options set, you automatically configure all EC2 instances to use your on-premises NTP server. No extra software or infrastructure is required. VPC DHCP Options Docs

w.y: "Least administrative overhead" means using a VPC-wide setting. A DHCP options set that lists the on-premises NTP server tells every instance which time source to use, assuming there is network connectivity to the data center.

o.A: Correct: a DHCP options set pushes the on-premises NTP server to all instances automatically.
o.B: Wrong: Amazon Time Sync is AWS's own time source, not the on-premises atomic clock.
o.C: Wrong: running a Marketplace NTP server adds servers to manage and does not use the required clock.
o.D: Wrong: a VPN only provides connectivity; instances still need to be told which NTP server to use.
